title: MAP Sensor (Vacuum) Circuit Malfunction
problem: The Engine Control Module (ECM) detects an abnormally low or high vacuum signal from the Manifold Absolute Pressure (MAP) sensor. This can indicate a vacuum leak or a sensor fault.
symptoms: Rough idle; Engine hesitation; Reduced power
actions: Check vacuum lines for leaks; Inspect MAP sensor connector; Test MAP sensor voltage
location: On the intake manifold, connected by a vacuum hose.

title: MAP Sensor (Voltage) Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects a voltage signal from the MAP sensor that is out of the expected operating range, indicating an electrical issue with the sensor or its wiring.
symptoms: Engine stalling; Difficulty starting; Poor fuel economy
actions: Check MAP sensor wiring for shorts/opens; Verify sensor power and ground; Replace MAP sensor if faulty
location: On the intake manifold, connected by a vacuum hose.

title: Engine Coolant Temperature (ECT) Sensor Malfunction
problem: The ECM receives an incorrect temperature reading from the ECT sensor, which is crucial for fuel mixture calculations and engine timing.
symptoms: Hard starting when cold/hot; Rich/lean running; Cooling fan issues
actions: Check sensor wiring and connector; Test sensor resistance at different temperatures; Replace ECT sensor
location: Screwed into the cylinder head or thermostat housing.

title: Throttle Position (TP) Sensor Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects an abnormal voltage output from the TP sensor, which measures the throttle plate's opening angle, affecting fuel delivery and ignition timing.
symptoms: Erratic idle; Engine surging; Loss of throttle response
actions: Inspect TP sensor wiring; Check sensor for proper calibration; Replace TP sensor if out of spec
location: Attached directly to the throttle body shaft.

title: Intake Air Temperature (IAT) Sensor Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects an incorrect temperature reading for the intake air, leading to inaccurate fuel mixture calculations.
symptoms: Poor fuel efficiency; Reduced power; Emissions issues
actions: Check IAT sensor wiring; Test sensor resistance; Replace IAT sensor
location: Located in the airbox or intake manifold.

title: Atmospheric Pressure (ATMP) Sensor Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects an abnormal atmospheric pressure reading, which is used for altitude compensation in fuel mapping.
symptoms: Reduced engine performance at varying altitudes; Excessive fuel consumption
actions: Inspect sensor wiring; Check sensor reading against known atmospheric pressure; Replace ATMP sensor
location: Often integrated into the ECM or located near it, sometimes on the airbox.

title: Vehicle Speed Sensor (VSS) Malfunction
problem: The ECM is not receiving a correct speed signal from the VSS, affecting speedometer operation, gear position indication, and sometimes limiting engine power.
symptoms: Speedometer not working; Cruise control failure; Engine 'limp mode'
actions: Check VSS wiring and connector; Inspect VSS for damage or debris; Replace VSS
location: On the transmission output shaft or front/rear wheel speed sensor (ABS type).

title: Fuel Injector No. 1 Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects an open or short circuit in the No. 1 fuel injector's electrical circuit, preventing proper fuel delivery to that cylinder.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Rough idle; Loss of power in one cylinder
actions: Check injector wiring and connector; Test injector resistance; Swap injector with another cylinder to confirm fault
location: Mounted in the throttle body or intake runner, above the intake valve for cylinder 1.

title: Fuel Injector No. 2 Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects an open or short circuit in the No. 2 fuel injector's electrical circuit, preventing proper fuel delivery to that cylinder.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Reduced power; Increased emissions
actions: Check injector wiring and connector; Test injector resistance; Inspect for fuel leaks
location: Mounted in the throttle body or intake runner, above the intake valve for cylinder 2.

title: Cam Pulse Generator (CMP) Sensor Malfunction
problem: The ECM is not receiving a proper signal from the CMP sensor, which synchronizes fuel injection and ignition timing with the camshaft position.
symptoms: Engine no-start; Cranks but no start; Misfire
actions: Inspect sensor wiring; Check sensor air gap and debris; Test sensor output signal
location: Located on the cylinder head, near the camshaft.

title: Bank Angle Sensor Malfunction
problem: The bank angle sensor detects the motorcycle's lean angle. A malfunction in its circuit can cause the engine to shut off as a safety measure.
symptoms: Engine cuts out unexpectedly; Engine will not start; Intermittent power loss
actions: Check sensor wiring; Verify sensor mounting orientation; Replace sensor if faulty
location: Typically mounted securely under the seat or near the front fairing.

title: Oxygen (O2) Sensor Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects an abnormal signal from the O2 sensor, which monitors exhaust gas oxygen content to adjust the fuel mixture.
symptoms: Poor fuel economy; Increased emissions; Reduced engine performance
actions: Inspect O2 sensor wiring; Check for exhaust leaks before the sensor; Replace O2 sensor
location: Screwed into the exhaust manifold or exhaust pipe before the catalytic converter.

title: O2 Sensor Heater Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects an open or short circuit in the O2 sensor's heater circuit, preventing the sensor from reaching its operating temperature quickly.
symptoms: Increased emissions
actions: especially on cold start; Poor fuel economy before warmup
location: Check heater circuit wiring; Test heater element resistance; Replace O2 sensor (heater is integrated)
column9: Integrated within the O2 sensor, screwed into the exhaust.

title: Knock Sensor Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects a malfunction in the knock sensor circuit, which listens for engine knocking/detonation and allows the ECM to retard ignition timing.
symptoms: Reduced engine power; Pre-ignition/detonation; Engine overheating
actions: Check sensor wiring and connector; Ensure sensor is properly torqued; Replace knock sensor
location: Bolted to the engine block or cylinder head.

title: Idle Air Control (IAC) Valve Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects an issue with the IAC valve circuit or its operation, preventing proper idle speed control.
symptoms: Erratic idle; Stalling at idle; High or low idle speed
actions: Clean IAC valve; Check valve wiring; Test valve operation with diagnostic tool
location: Mounted on or near the throttle body.

title: ECM Internal Error (EEPROM/CPU)
problem: A detected internal error within the ECM's memory or processing unit, indicating a severe malfunction of the control unit itself.
symptoms: Engine no-start; Intermittent power loss; Multiple unrelated DTCs
actions: Check ECM power and ground; Verify ECM connectors; ECM replacement may be required
location: Typically located under the seat, behind a side panel, or in the fairing.

title: Exhaust Gas Control Valve (EGCV) Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects an issue with the exhaust valve control system, often indicating a problem with the motor or cables that operate the valve in the exhaust pipe.
symptoms: Reduced high-RPM power; Erratic exhaust note; Check engine light
actions: Inspect valve cables for binding; Check EGCV motor wiring; Recalibrate or replace EGCV motor
location: EGCV motor usually under the seat or side panel, connected by cables to the valve in the exhaust.

title: Secondary Air Supply Solenoid Valve (PAIR) Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects a malfunction in the Secondary Air Injection (PAIR) system solenoid valve, which injects fresh air into the exhaust to burn unburnt hydrocarbons.
symptoms: Increased emissions; Slightly reduced fuel economy; No noticeable performance impact
actions: Check solenoid wiring and connector; Test solenoid operation; Inspect PAIR system hoses for leaks
location: Located on the engine
column9: connected to the airbox and exhaust ports.

title: Fuel Pump Relay Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects an issue with the fuel pump relay circuit, preventing the fuel pump from receiving power.
symptoms: Engine no-start; Engine stalls; No fuel pump prime sound
actions: Check relay wiring; Test relay continuity; Replace fuel pump relay
location: Typically located in the fuse box or near the battery.

title: ABS System Malfunction
affectedPart: ABS Control Unit / Wheel Speed Sensor
problem: The Anti-lock Braking System (ABS) control unit detects an internal fault or an issue with one of its wheel speed sensors, disabling the ABS function.
symptoms: ABS warning light on; Brakes feel normal but without ABS; Hard braking can lock wheels
actions: Check wheel speed sensor wiring; Clean wheel speed sensors; Perform ABS diagnostic procedure
location: ABS control unit usually under the seat; Wheel speed sensors at each wheel.

title: Throttle By Wire (TBW) System Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects a malfunction in the electronic throttle control system, which controls the throttle plate without a physical cable.
symptoms: No throttle response; Engine enters 'limp home' mode; Erratic engine speed
actions: Inspect TBW sensor wiring; Check throttle plate for binding; Recalibrate or replace TBW components
location: TBW sensors/actuator integrated with the throttle body.

title: Electronic Throttle Control System (ETCS) Relay Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects an issue with the ETCS relay circuit, which supplies power to the electronic throttle control system components.
symptoms: Engine no-start; No throttle response; Engine stalls
actions: Check ETCS relay wiring; Test relay functionality; Replace ETCS relay
location: Typically located in the fuse box or near the battery.

title: Electronic Throttle Control System (ETCS) Motor Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects a malfunction in the ETCS motor that physically moves the throttle plate.
symptoms: No throttle response; Engine enters 'limp home' mode; Check engine light and reduced power
actions: Inspect ETCS motor wiring; Check throttle body for obstructions; Replace throttle body assembly if motor is integrated
location: Integrated into the throttle body assembly.

title: MAP Sensor Circuit Low Input
problem: The ECM detects a voltage signal from the MAP sensor that is consistently lower than the expected range, indicating a potential sensor failure or wiring issue (e.g., short to ground).
symptoms: Engine hesitation; Poor acceleration; Rich fuel mixture
actions: Check MAP sensor wiring for shorts; Test sensor voltage output; Replace MAP sensor if readings are incorrect
location: On the intake manifold, connected by a vacuum hose.

title: MAP Sensor Circuit High Input
problem: The ECM detects a voltage signal from the MAP sensor that is consistently higher than the expected range, indicating a potential sensor failure or wiring issue (e.g., open circuit or short to power).
symptoms: Rough idle; Lean fuel mixture; Reduced engine power
actions: Check MAP sensor wiring for opens; Test sensor voltage output; Verify vacuum line integrity
location: On the intake manifold, connected by a vacuum hose.

title: IAT Sensor Circuit High Input
problem: The ECM detects a voltage signal from the IAT sensor that is consistently higher than expected, suggesting an open circuit or faulty sensor reading cold.
symptoms: Rich fuel mixture; Reduced fuel economy; Hard starting in warm weather
actions: Check IAT sensor wiring for opens; Test sensor resistance; Replace IAT sensor
location: Located in the airbox or intake manifold.

title: ECT Sensor Circuit High Input
problem: The ECM detects a voltage signal from the ECT sensor that is consistently higher than expected, indicating an open circuit or a faulty sensor reading cold.
symptoms: Engine runs rich; Overheating potential; Poor cold start performance
actions: Check ECT sensor wiring for opens; Test sensor resistance; Replace ECT sensor
location: Screwed into the cylinder head or thermostat housing.

title: TP Sensor Circuit Low Input
problem: The ECM detects a voltage signal from the TP sensor that is consistently lower than the expected range, often indicating a short to ground or a faulty sensor.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response; Engine stalls; Erratic idle
actions: Check TP sensor wiring for shorts; Verify sensor power and ground; Adjust or replace TP sensor
location: Attached directly to the throttle body shaft.

title: TP Sensor Circuit High Input
problem: The ECM detects a voltage signal from the TP sensor that is consistently higher than the expected range, often indicating an open circuit or faulty sensor.
symptoms: Engine surging; Poor acceleration; Limp home mode
actions: Check TP sensor wiring for opens; Verify sensor calibration; Replace TP sensor
location: Attached directly to the throttle body shaft.

title: System Too Lean (Bank 1)
problem: The ECM detects that the engine is running consistently too lean (too much air, not enough fuel) in Bank 1, often due to vacuum leaks, low fuel pressure, or faulty O2 sensor.
symptoms: Engine hesitation; Poor acceleration; Hard starting
actions: Check for vacuum leaks; Inspect fuel pressure; Test O2 sensor functionality
location: Engine compartment, affecting intake manifold, fuel lines, or exhaust.

title: System Too Rich (Bank 1)
problem: The ECM detects that the engine is running consistently too rich (too much fuel, not enough air) in Bank 1, often due to leaky injectors, high fuel pressure, or faulty O2 sensor.
symptoms: Poor fuel economy; Black smoke from exhaust; Rough idle
actions: Check fuel injectors for leaks; Verify fuel pressure regulator; Test O2 sensor functionality
location: Engine compartment, affecting fuel injectors, fuel lines, or exhaust.

title: Injector Circuit Malfunction - Cylinder 1
problem: The ECM detects an electrical fault (open or short) in the control circuit for the fuel injector of cylinder 1.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Reduced power; Engine running on fewer cylinders
actions: Check injector harness continuity; Test injector resistance; Swap injector to verify fault
location: Mounted in the throttle body or intake runner, above the intake valve for cylinder 1.

title: Fuel Pump Primary Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects an electrical fault in the primary control circuit for the fuel pump relay, preventing the fuel pump from operating.
symptoms: Engine no-start; Cranks but no start; No fuel pump prime sound
actions: Check fuel pump relay wiring; Test fuel pump relay; Inspect fuse for fuel pump
location: Fuel pump relay typically in fuse box; Fuel pump in the fuel tank.

title: Crankshaft Position (CKP) Sensor 'A' Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECM is not receiving a proper signal from the CKP sensor, which is essential for determining engine speed and piston position for ignition and fuel timing.
symptoms: Engine no-start; Cranks but no start; Intermittent engine cut-out
actions: Inspect sensor wiring; Check sensor for metallic debris; Test sensor output signal
location: Mounted near the crankshaft, usually on the engine case, often behind a cover.

title: Camshaft Position (CMP) Sensor Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECM is not receiving a proper signal from the CMP sensor, which synchronizes fuel injection and ignition timing with the camshaft position.
symptoms: Engine no-start; Cranks but no start; Misfire
actions: Inspect sensor wiring; Check sensor air gap and debris; Test sensor output signal
location: Located on the cylinder head, near the camshaft.

title: Vehicle Speed Sensor (VSS) Malfunction
problem: The ECM is not receiving a correct speed signal from the VSS, affecting speedometer operation and various engine management functions.
symptoms: Speedometer not working; Inconsistent idle; Poor gear shifts (automatic)
actions: Check VSS wiring and connector; Inspect VSS for damage or debris; Replace VSS
location: On the transmission output shaft or front/rear wheel speed sensor (ABS type).

title: Idle Control System RPM Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects that the engine idle speed is not within the specified range, often due to issues with the Idle Air Control system or vacuum leaks.
symptoms: Unstable idle; Engine stalls when coming to a stop; High idle
actions: Check for vacuum leaks; Clean IAC valve; Adjust idle screw (if applicable)
location: IAC valve on or near the throttle body; Vacuum lines around the intake manifold.

title: System Voltage Malfunction
problem: The ECM detects that the motorcycle's system voltage is outside the normal operating range, indicating issues with the battery or charging system.
symptoms: Dim lights; Battery not charging; Engine difficult to start
actions: Check battery voltage and terminals; Test rectifier/regulator; Inspect stator output
location: Battery under the seat; Rectifier/regulator typically near the battery or under a side panel; Stator inside the left engine cover.

title: Internal Control Module Memory Check Sum Error
problem: The ECM has detected an internal error in its read-only memory (ROM) or random-access memory (RAM), indicating a fundamental fault within the ECM itself.
symptoms: Engine no-start; Intermittent engine operation; Multiple unrelated DTCs
actions: Check ECM power and ground connections; Inspect for moisture ingress at ECM; ECM replacement often required
location: Typically located under the seat, behind a side panel, or in the fairing.

title: ECM Internal Circuit Malfunction
problem: A Honda-specific P-code indicating an internal fault or processing error within the ECM. This can affect various engine management functions.
symptoms: Engine no-start; Intermittent power loss; Erratic engine behavior
actions: Check ECM connectors for corrosion; Verify all ECM power/ground wires; ECM replacement typically needed
location: Typically located under the seat, behind a side panel, or in the fairing.

title: ECM Internal Circuit Malfunction - Sensor Power
affectedPart: Engine Control Module (ECM) / Sensor Power Supply
problem: A Honda-specific P-code indicating an internal fault within the ECM related to its ability to supply stable reference voltage to various sensors.
symptoms: Multiple sensor-related DTCs; Engine no-start; Engine stalls
actions: Check for shorted sensor wiring; Verify ECM power/ground; ECM replacement typically needed
location: Typically located under the seat, behind a side panel, or in the fairing.

title: MIL Control Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECM has detected an issue with the circuit that controls the Malfunction Indicator Lamp, meaning the 'Check Engine' light itself might not be functioning correctly.
symptoms: MIL light not illuminating when it should; MIL light staying on constantly; No clear diagnostic indication
actions: Check MIL bulb/LED; Inspect MIL wiring harness; Test ECM output to MIL
location: Instrument cluster.
